//! Shapes an exclusion declaration has to scope over in Rust: a free function,
//! a method in an impl block, a generic, a closure and a nested fn item.

/// Adds two numbers, and every test covers it.
pub fn add(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    a + b
}

/// Shells out to a foreign toolchain, so no unit test runs it.
// [lydite:exclude_from_coverage][it invokes a foreign toolchain; the proving
// ground exercises it]
pub fn provision(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    if name.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("anonymous");
    } else {
        out.push_str(name);
    }
    out.push_str("-provisioned");
    out
}

/// Generic, so llvm-cov records one instantiation per type argument.
pub fn widest<T: PartialOrd + Copy>(items: &[T]) -> Option<T> {
    let mut best: Option<T> = None;
    for item in items {
        match best {
            Some(b) if b >= *item => {}
            _ => best = Some(*item),
        }
    }
    best
}

/// Holds a closure, whose lines belong to the function that declares it.
pub fn tally(items: &[i64]) -> i64 {
    let double = |n: &i64| {
        let d = n * 2;
        d
    };
    items.iter().map(double).sum()
}

/// Holds a nested fn item, which is its own symbol.
pub fn outer(n: i64) -> i64 {
    fn inner(n: i64) -> i64 {
        n * 3
    }
    inner(n)
}

/// A counter whose methods share one impl block.
pub struct Counter {
    value: i64,
}

impl Counter {
    /// Starts at zero.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Counter { value: 0 }
    }

    /// Adds one.
    pub fn bump(&mut self) {
        self.value += 1;
    }

    /// Never called by any test.
    // [lydite:exclude_from_coverage][the value is read only by the binary]
    pub fn value(&self) -> i64 {
        self.value
    }
}

impl Default for Counter {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn add_sums() {
        assert_eq!(add(2, 3), 5);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bump_increments() {
        let mut c = Counter::new();
        c.bump();
    }

    #[test]
    fn widest_over_two_types() {
        assert_eq!(widest(&[1i64, 7, 3]), Some(7));
        assert_eq!(widest(&[1.5f64, 0.5]), Some(1.5));
    }

    #[test]
    fn tally_doubles() {
        assert_eq!(tally(&[1, 2, 3]), 12);
    }

    #[test]
    fn outer_triples() {
        assert_eq!(outer(2), 6);
    }
}
